مُسْتَلْفَجٌ , (as in the K,) or ↓ مُسْتَلْفِجٌ , (as in the L [and this latter I think the correct mode of writing the word in all the senses here explained, for I do not find it noted as extr. with respect to rule like مُلْفَجٌ,]) [part. n. of 10, q. v.: and] i. q. مُلْفَجٌ, q. v. (K.) ―
-b2- One whose heart forsakes him, or fails him, by reason of fear, or fright. (K.) ―
-b3- Cleaving to the ground by reason of emaciation, (K,) or of sorrow, grief, or solicitude, or of want; as also ملفج [i. e. مُلْفِجٌ and مُلْفَجٌ: see 4]. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
